name: aqsoldb
preregistration_note: Drafted 2026-10-21 before any run on this dataset; only the CSV header was inspected. Same property as ESOL, so the control and baseline are ESOL's, fixed a priori; noise floor from the cited literature; cf_threshold follows the fixed rule 5/3 x noise floor rounded to 0.1. AqSolDB merges nine sources and likely overlaps ESOL's molecules, so it tests generality across data more than independence from ESOL.

source.citation: Sorkun, Khetan & Er 2019, Sci. Data, PMID 31395888 (AqSolDB)

noise_floor_source: Palmer & Mitchell 2014, Mol. Pharm., PMID 24919008: literature solubility data carry 'experimental uncertainty ... estimated to be 0.6-0.7 log S units'; Llinas & Avdeef 2019 (PMID 31042031): ~0.62 log for loosely curated shake-flask data.

control.name: lipophilicity
control.rationale: logS is dominated by lipophilicity; the ESOL equation's largest term is cLogP.

baseline.text: Molecules with LogP above the training median ({value:.2f}) are less soluble.
Molecules heavier than the training median ({value:.0f} Da) are less soluble.
Molecules with two or more aromatic rings are less soluble.
Molecules with sp3 fraction above the training median ({value:.2f}) are more soluble.
Molecules with at least one hydrogen-bond donor are more soluble.
